metadata.chunk_title: Bachelor of Business Studies (BBS) with Spanish (beginners or advanced)

programme_facts.value: This module is taught to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) standard. The beginner's module aims to provide the student with a strong basic knowledge of Spanish and of contemporary Spain and Latin America, particularly as regards the economic and commercial dimensions. The module is designed to enable the student to understand and use basic structures of Spanish grammar, expose the student to a range of vocabulary and expressions which will allow her/him to present her/himself to, and communicate with native speakers of Spanish, foster autonomous language learning skills, introduce the student to Spanish and Latin American cultures, develop listening and speaking skills in Spanish, and equip the student with basic writing skills.

metadata.chunk_title: Beginners Spanish + Advanced Spanish

programme_facts.value: This module is taught to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) standard to introduce students to Business Spanish relevant to their future professional needs, provide students with an understanding of key aspects of contemporary Spanish society, enable students to develop practical skills (receptive and active), and consolidate students' knowledge of Spanish vocabulary and grammar.

programme_facts.value: The aim of this module is to develop a student's understanding of the theory and practice of selected international accounting standards. It encourages the student to critically evaluate selected accounting standards in light of their historical development and regulatory context.

metadata.chunk_title: Module Code - Title: + Year Last Offered: + Hours Per Week: + Grading Type: + Prerequisite Modules: + Rationale and Purpose of the Module:

programme_facts.value: The module will consider the theory and practice of selected international accounting standards and issues. Focus will be on the preparation and reporting of information to external users of financial information, especially, but not exclusively, equity investors. The international accounting standards and issues are examined in light of their historical development and discussions will not be solely around the actual content but what the regulations ought to be or might be. The module will cover the International Financial Reporting Standards.
